questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 4 hours, B and C together in 3 hours, and A and C together in 2 hours. How long will B alone take to do it ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a piece of work in 4 hours.

B and C together can do it in 3 hours.

A and C together can do it in 2 hours.

**Concept used:**

Work done = 1/Time Or Work done = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

A can do a piece of work in 4 hours.

A's 1-hour work = 1/4

A and C together can do it in 2 hours.

(A + C)'s 1-hour work = 1/2

C's 1 hour work = 1/2 - 1/4

⇒ 1/4

B and C together can do it in 3 hours.

(B + C)'s 1-hour work = 1/3

B's 1-hour work = 1/3 - 1/4

⇒ 1/12

Time taken by B to complete the work = 12 hours

**∴ The time taken by B to complete the work is 12 hours.**

questions.question: If a = 2⁴ × 3 × 5³; b = 2³ × 5² & c = 3³ × 5² × 7, then HCF (a, b, c) = ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the HCF from prime factorized numbers, identify the prime base common to all given numbers.

Only the prime base 5 is present in all three numbers (a, b, and c).

The smallest power of 5 among the given numbers is 5².

HCF = 5² = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

a = 2⁴ × 3 × 5³

b = 2³ × 5²

c = 3³ × 5² × 7

**Formula Used:**

The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the product of the lowest powers of all common prime factors present in the numbers.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Identify the prime factors present in all three numbers a, b, and c.

⇒ Factor 2 is present in a and b, but missing in c.

⇒ Factor 3 is present in a and c, but missing in b.

⇒ Factor 7 is present only in c.

⇒ The only common prime factor in all three numbers is 5.

⇒ Find the lowest power of 5 present in the numbers:

⇒ Power of 5 in a = 3

⇒ Power of 5 in b = 2

⇒ Power of 5 in c = 2

⇒ The minimum power of 5 among them is 2.

⇒ HCF(a, b, c) = 5²

⇒ HCF(a, b, c) = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Numbers in Prime Factor Form

The Least Common Multiple (LCM) is found by multiplying the highest powers of all prime factors present in any of the given numbers. For the given a, b, and c, LCM = 2⁴ × 3³ × 5³ × 7.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM (A × B = HCF × LCM). This rule strictly applies to two numbers only and is not valid for three or more numbers.

Co-Prime Numbers

If the HCF of two or more numbers is 1, they are called co-prime numbers. They do not share any common prime factors other than 1 (for example, 8 and 15).

questions.question: A car travels 1/3 of the distance on a straight road with a speed of 10 km/h, next 1/3 with a speed of 20 km/h and last 1/3 with 60 km/h. What would be the average speed of the car for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Car travels 1st 1/3rd of total distance with speed = 10 km/h

Car travels 2nd 1/3rd of total distance with speed = 20 km/h

Car travels 3rd 1/3rd of total distance with speed = 60 km/h

**Concept used:**

Speed = distance / time

Average speed = total distance travelled / total time taken

**Calculation:**

Let the total distance be 3x km.

Time taken by car to travel 1st 1/3rd of total distance or (1/3) × 3x = x km distance

Speed = distance / time

10 = x / time

time = x / 10

Time taken by car to travel 2nd 1/3rd of total distance or (1/3) × 3x = x km distance

Speed = distance / time

20 = x / time

time = x / 20

Time taken by car to travel 3rd 1/3rd of total distance or (1/3) × 3x = x km distance

Speed = distance / time

60 = x / time

time = x / 60

Average speed of the car

= Total distance travelled / total time taken

= dfrac{3x}{dfrac{x}{10} + dfrac {x}{20} + dfrac {x}{60}}

= dfrac{3x}{dfrac{6x + 3x + x}{60}}

= 180x / 10x

= 18 km/hr.

**∴ The average speed of the car is 18 km/hr.**

questions.question: In a business venture, the investment made by A is 75% of the investment made by B, while the investment made by C is 120% of the investment made by B. The time period of investment made by A is twice the time period of B, which is in turn thrice of the time period of C. Find the difference between the return accrued to A and C if the profit accrued at the end of the year is Rs 10,150.
questions.solution:
Concept: 

In a business, the profits are shared in the ratio of the product of the sum and the time for which the sum is invested for each of the partners. Hence, the product of Investment (I) and time (T) is always in proportion to the profits obtained (P). 

⇒ P = I × T 

**Calculation:**

Let the investment made by B be "b" and the time period of investment for C be "t".

⇒ Investment made by A = 0.75 × b = 0.75b

⇒ Investment made by C = 1.2 × b = 1.2b

⇒ Time period of investment made by B = 3 × t = 3t

⇒ Time period of investment made by A = 2 × 3t = 6t

∴ Ratio of investment at the end of year = 0.75b × 6t : b × 3t : 1.2b × t = 4.5 : 3 : 1.2

Multiplying the ratio by 10 and reducing them to the lowest form, we get

⇒ Ratio of profit = 15 : 10 : 4

The difference between the ratio of profit for A and C = 15 - 4 = 11

⇒ Actual difference = 11over29 × Rs 10,150 = Rs 3,850

**The difference in the profit is Rs 3,850.**

questions.question: A person buys a car at 25% discount on the marked price and sells it at 20% higher than the marked price. What is the actual gain percentage?

Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100 units.

Cost Price (CP) after 25% discount = 100 − 25 = 75 units.

Selling Price (SP) at 20% higher than MP = 100 + 20 = 120 units.

Actual Profit = SP − CP = 120 − 75 = 45 units.

B. It suggests that perceiving adversity as opportunity is central to Stoic philosophy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Supported by the passage:**

The passage states:

"The Stoics themselves believed in gods, but ultimately those resistant to religious belief can take their Stoicism the way they take their Buddhism, even if they can’t buy into such concepts as karma or reincarnation."

This shows that Stoicism can be practiced and valued even without religious belief.

 

**B. It suggests that perceiving adversity as opportunity is central to Stoic philosophy.**

**Supported by the passage:**

The passage says:

"This is one of the truly great mind-hacks ever devised, this willingness to convert adversity to opportunity, and it’s part of what Seneca was extolling..."

This makes clear that viewing adversity as opportunity is a core Stoic idea.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The passage actually challenges positive thinking and promotes “negative visualisation” as a Stoic technique:

"By keeping the very worst that can happen in our heads constantly, the Stoics tell us, we immunise ourselves from the dangers of too much so-called 'positive thinking'..."

It presents negative visualisation as preferable to uncritical positive thinking, not the other way around.

The author describes how the "vision of reality as something generative – perpetually changing for the benefit and flourishing of all it creates – has dominated Western philosophy," and that "all that is wrong might be put to rights... if only we could find a way to live within the purely creative and inherently benevolent order of existence." However, the passage then challenges this by saying these assumptions "are no longer tenable," implying that believing in the Universe's inherent benevolence may lead us to underestimate or misunderstand the consequences and responsibilities of our environmental actions.

C) The author believes that all human actions, no matter how destructive, align with a broader cosmic process.

**Supported by the passage**:

In the final lines, the author states that "our most excessive actions as a species – destroying rainforests, causing widespread extinction... – are perfectly in keeping with the ultimate aims of the Universe." This means that even destructive actions are seen as part of the Universe's ongoing process, challenging the notion that the Universe is inherently benevolent or that human destructiveness is somehow "unnatural."

However, it does not explicitly say that aligning with nature is “no longer a relevant ethical guide.” Rather, the passage questions whether our former understanding of nature as inherently benevolent and creative is sufficient, but it does not completely dismiss the relevance of aligning with nature as an ethical guide. It complicates the idea, but does not make the sweeping claim that it is entirely irrelevant.

C. The passage presents the idea that human-caused environmental destruction is fundamentally opposed to the Universe’s aims.

questions.question: Who appoints a special officer for linguistic minorities to investigate all matters relating to the constitutional safeguards for linguistic minorities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

__
 
• The President of India should appoint a special officer for linguistic minorities. 
 
• This officer investigates all matters relating to the constitutional safeguards for linguistic minorities and also reports to the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Originally, the Constitution of India did not make any provision with respect to the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. Later, the States Reorganization Commission (1953-55) made a recommendation in this regard. 
 
• Accordingly, the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 inserted a new Article 350-B in Part XVII of the Constitution.
 
• **This article contains the following provisions: **
 
 
• There should be a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. 
 
• He is to be appointed by the President of India.
 
• It would be the duty of the Special Officer to investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution.
 
• He would report to the President upon those matters at such intervals as the President may direct. 
 
• The President should place all such reports before each House of Parliament and send them to the governments of the states concerned.
 
• It must be noted here that the Constitution does not specify the qualifications, tenure, salaries and allowances, service conditions, and procedure for removal of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements :

1. Prokaryotes store their DNA only in the cytoplasm.

2. Cellular organisms use messenger RNA (mRNA) to convey genetic information that directs the synthesis of specific proteins.

3. A DNA molecule is capable of self-duplication during cell division and identical DNA strands are transferred to daughter cells.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Eukaryotic organisms (animals, plants, fungi, and protists) store most of their DNA inside the cell nucleus and some of their DNA in organelles, such as mitochondria or chloroplasts.
 
• In contrast,** prokaryotes (bacteria and archaea) store their DNA only in the cytoplasm. Hence statement 1 is correct.**
 
• DNA is the chemical basis of heredity and has the coded message for proteins to be synthesized in the cell.
 
 
• There are three types of RNA — mRNA, rRNA and tRNA which actually carry out the protein synthesis in the cell based on the coded message for proteins provided by DNA.
 
• Ribonucleic acid (RNA) is implicated in various biological roles in coding, decoding, regulation, and expression of genes.
 
• **Cellular organisms use messenger RNA (mRNA) to convey genetic information that directs the synthesis of specific proteins. Hence statement 2 is correct.**
 
• Many viruses encode their genetic information using an RNA genome.
 
• Example: HIV virus used this technique to proliferate within the human body.
 
 
 
• DNA is the chemical basis of heredity and may be regarded as the reserve of genetic information.
 
 
• DNA is exclusively responsible for maintaining the identity of different species of organisms over millions of years.
 
• **A DNA molecule is capable of self-duplication during cell division and identical DNA strands are transferred to daughter cells. Hence statement 3 is correct.**
 
• Another important function of nucleic acids in protein synthesis in the cell. Actually, the proteins are synthesized by various RNA molecules in the cell but the message for the synthesis of a particular protein is present in DNA.

questions.question: A CPU has 32 bit program counter. This means that the CPU can address:

• CPU with a 32-bit program counter can address approximately 4 gigabytes (GB) of memory locations.
 
• The number of memory locations that can be addressed by a CPU is determined by the width of the address bus. In this case, a CPU with a 32-bit program counter can address 2^32 (2 raised to the power of 32) memory locations.
 
• Each memory location typically represents 1 byte of data. So, with a 32-bit program counter, the CPU can address a total of 4,294,967,296 (2^32) memory locations, which is equivalent to 4 gigabytes of addressable memory (assuming each memory location represents 1 byte).
 
• It's important to note that the actual amount of memory that can be used by a system may be less than 4GB due to various factors, including system architecture, operating system limitations, and reserved memory for hardware or system purposes.

• **Text group:** As mentioned earlier, this group contains commands for adding and formatting text. This includes Text Box, Header & Footer, WordArt, Date & Time, Slide Number, and Object (in some versions). The Text Box tool lets you add a box in which you can type text. The Header & Footer tool allows you to add information like the date, slide number, or additional text at the top (header) or bottom (footer) of your slides.
 
• **Tables group:** This group contains commands that** let you insert and format tables in your slides.** A table can be a useful way to present structured information, like numerical data or a schedule. After clicking the Table button, you can specify the number of rows and columns you want your table to have.
